safe_variant_proposals.topic: Capital received on forfeited premium shares
safe_variant_proposals.stem: A company forfeits fully called-up shares of Rs 10 each issued at a premium of Rs 2 each. All amounts due, including premium, had been received except the final call of Rs 4 per share. The Share Forfeiture Account is credited with Rs 5,400. How many shares were forfeited?
safe_variant_proposals.explanation: Paid share capital is Rs 10 - Rs 4 = Rs 6 per share. Received premium is excluded from forfeiture credit. Rs 5,400 / Rs 6 = 900 shares.
explicit_assumptions: Only the stated final call unpaid

safe_variant_proposals.topic: Forfeiture entry where premium due remains unpaid
safe_variant_proposals.stem: A company forfeits 200 fully called-up shares of Rs 10 each issued at a premium of Rs 3. The company received Rs 4 per share towards capital on application. The allotment of Rs 5 per share (including the entire Rs 3 premium) and the final call of Rs 4 per share remain unpaid. Premium had been credited when allotment became due. A separate Calls in Arrears Account includes all unpaid allotment and call amounts. Match the accounts with the forfeiture entry amounts. List I: (A) Share Capital debit; (B) Securities Premium debit; (C) Calls in Arrears credit; (D) Share Forfeiture credit. List II: (I) Rs 800; (II) Rs 600; (III) Rs 2,000; (IV) Rs 1,800.
safe_variant_proposals.explanation: Capital debit is 200 x Rs 10 = Rs 2,000; unpaid premium debit is 200 x Rs 3 = Rs 600. Unpaid allotment and call total 200 x (Rs 5 + Rs 4) = Rs 1,800. Paid capital credit is 200 x Rs 4 = Rs 800. Both entry sides total Rs 2,600.
explicit_assumptions: All call amounts stated reconcile to face capital plus premium
Premium credited on due entry but never received
Calls in Arrears includes the unpaid premium component

safe_variant_proposals.stem: A firm uses fixed capital accounts. R's Current Account opens with a credit balance of Rs 12,000. During the year R is credited with salary Rs 18,000, interest on capital Rs 6,000 and a share of residual profit Rs 24,000. R withdraws Rs 15,000 for personal use and is charged interest on drawings Rs 1,000. R also introduces Rs 40,000 as additional permanent capital. There are no other entries. What is R's closing Current Account balance?
safe_variant_proposals.explanation: Current credits total Rs 12,000 + Rs 18,000 + Rs 6,000 + Rs 24,000 = Rs 60,000. Current debits are Rs 16,000. The closing balance is Rs 44,000 credit. Additional permanent capital is recorded in Capital Account.
explicit_assumptions: Salary and interest are already allowed

safe_variant_proposals.topic: Residual-profit transfer to fixed-method current accounts
safe_variant_proposals.stem: A and B maintain fixed capital accounts and share profits 3:2. After every other appropriation has been recorded, Rs 75,000 of profit remains to be distributed. Which entry records only this residual-profit transfer?
options: P&L Appropriation Dr Rs 75,000; A Current Cr Rs 45,000; B Current Cr Rs 30,000
A Current Dr Rs 45,000; B Current Dr Rs 30,000; P&L Appropriation Cr Rs 75,000
P&L Appropriation Dr Rs 75,000; A Capital Cr Rs 45,000; B Capital Cr Rs 30,000
P&L Dr Rs 75,000; A Current Cr Rs 45,000; B Current Cr Rs 30,000
safe_variant_proposals.explanation: Residual profit is transferred by debiting P&L Appropriation and crediting the partners in their agreed shares. Rs 75,000 x 3/5 = Rs 45,000 and x 2/5 = Rs 30,000. Fixed capital requires the Current Accounts.

safe_variant_proposals.topic: Share-capital definitions, distinct from balance-sheet headings
safe_variant_proposals.stem: Match the share-capital terms with their meanings. List I: (A) Calls in arrears; (B) Calls in advance; (C) Reserve capital; (D) Securities premium. List II: (I) A portion of uncalled capital reserved to be called only on winding up; (II) Share amounts called but unpaid; (III) Excess of issue price over nominal value; (IV) Amount received from a shareholder before the corresponding call is made.
safe_variant_proposals.explanation: Arrears are called but unpaid amounts. Advance is received before its call. Reserve capital is a reserved portion of uncalled capital callable only on winding up. Securities premium is only the excess over nominal value.
explicit_assumptions: Only the premium excess is classified as securities premium

safe_variant_proposals.topic: Called-up capital less calls in arrears
safe_variant_proposals.stem: A company has allotted 12,000 shares of Rs 10 each and called Rs 8 per share. All called amounts have been received except a call of Rs 3 per share on 2,000 of these shares. No money has been received in advance and no shares have been forfeited. What is paid-up share capital?
safe_variant_proposals.explanation: Called-up capital is 12,000 x Rs 8 = Rs 96,000. Calls in arrears are 2,000 x Rs 3 = Rs 6,000. Paid-up capital is Rs 90,000; uncalled face capital is not included.
explicit_assumptions: Allotted shares and called amount explicit

safe_variant_proposals.topic: Excess applications as percentage of shares offered
safe_variant_proposals.stem: A company offers 48,000 shares for subscription and receives valid applications for 60,000 shares. Express the excess applications as a percentage of the number of shares offered. By what percentage is the offer oversubscribed?
safe_variant_proposals.explanation: Excess applications are 60,000 - 48,000 = 12,000. Relative to 48,000 shares offered, 12,000/48,000 x 100 = 25%. The 125% figure is total applications, not the excess.

safe_variant_proposals.topic: Calls in advance receipt, not later call adjustment
safe_variant_proposals.stem: A company authorised to accept calls in advance receives Rs 1,000 from a shareholder towards a future call which has not yet been made. Which entry records only this receipt?
options: Calls in Advance Dr Rs 1,000; Bank Cr Rs 1,000
Bank Dr Rs 1,000; Share Capital Cr Rs 1,000
Bank Dr Rs 1,000; Calls in Advance Cr Rs 1,000
Calls in Advance Dr Rs 1,000; Share Call Cr Rs 1,000
safe_variant_proposals.explanation: Bank is debited for cash received. Because the call has not been made, Calls in Advance is credited as a liability. Adjustment against a call due occurs later.

safe_variant_proposals.topic: Position in the profit-transfer and presentation chain
safe_variant_proposals.stem: A partnership traces profit from the Trading Account through final presentation in the Balance Sheet, including the partners' accounts after appropriation. Match each account with its position in that forward chain. List I: (A) Trading Account; (B) Profit and Loss Appropriation Account; (C) Balance Sheet; (D) Profit and Loss Account; (E) Partners' Capital/Current Accounts. List II: (I) First; (II) Second; (III) Third; (IV) Fourth; (V) Fifth.
safe_variant_proposals.explanation: The forward profit-transfer chain is Trading -> P&L -> P&L Appropriation -> partners' Capital/Current Accounts -> Balance Sheet. These are positions in the requested profit chain, not a claim that bookkeeping happens only in this temporal order.

trimmed_source_facts.exact_normalized_source_paragraph: Reserve Capital: A company may reserve a portion of its uncalled capital to be called only in the event of winding up of the company. Such uncalled amount is called ‘Reserve Capital’ of the company. It is available only for the creditors on winding up of the company.
supports: Reserve capital is a portion of uncalled capital callable only on winding up

trimmed_source_facts.exact_normalized_source_paragraph: (a) Fixed Capital Method: Under the fixed capital method, the capitals of the partners shall remain fixed unless additional capital is introduced or a part of the capital is withdrawn as per the agreement among the partners. All items like share of profit or loss, interest on capital, drawings, interest on drawings, etc. are recorded in a separate accounts, called Partner’s Current Account. The partners’ capital accounts will always show a credit balance, which shall remain the same (fixed) year after year unless there is any addition or withdrawal of capital. The partners’ current account on the other hand, may show a debit or a credit balance. Thus under this method, two accounts are maintained for each partner viz., capital account and current account, While the partners’ capital accounts shall always appear on the liabilities side in the balance sheet, the partners’ current account’s balance shall be shown on the liabilities side, if they have credit balance and on the assets side, if they have debit balance.
supports: Permanent capital changes versus current-account entries
trimmed_source_facts.excluded_context: Leading (v) and (vi) on this page continue a true/false exercise. They falsely claim default drawings interest 6% and partner loan interest 12%. Never treat these exercise statements as rules.

trimmed_source_facts.exact_normalized_source_block: 1.6.2 Calls in Advance Sometimes shareholders pay a part or the whole of the amount of the calls not yet made. The amount so received from the shareholders is known as “Calls in Advance”. The amount received in advance is a liability of the company and should be credited to ‘Call in Advance Account.” The amount received will be adjusted towards the payment of calls as and when they becomes due. Table F of the Companies Act provides for the payment of interest on calls in advance at a rate not exceeding 12% per annum. The following journal entry is recorded for the amount of calls received in advance. Bank A/c Dr. To Calls in Advance A/c (Amount received on call in advance)
supports: Bank Dr / Calls in Advance Cr

trimmed_source_facts.exact_normalized_source_paragraph: 1.6.3 Over Subscription There are instances when applications for more shares of a company are received than the number offered to the public for subscription. This usually happens in respect of shares issue of well-managed and financially strong companies and is said to be a case of ‘Over Subscription’.
supports: Applications compared with shares offered for subscription

trimmed_source_facts.section: Forfeiture of Shares issued at a Premium, paid/unpaid distinction
trimmed_source_facts.exact_normalized_source_paragraphs: Forfeiture of Shares issued at a Premium: If shares were initially issued at a premium and the premium amount has been fully realised, but some of the shares are forfeited due to non-payment of call money, the accounting treatment for forfeiture shall be on the same pattern as in the case of shares issued at par. The important point to be noted in this context is that the securities premium account is not to be debited at the time of forfeiture if the premium has been received in respect of the forefeited shares and the amount of forfeiture shall be excluding premium amount. In case, however, if the premium amount has not been received, either wholly or partially, in respect of the shares forfeited, the Securities Premium Reserve Account will also be debited with the amount of premium not received along with the Share Capital Account at the time forfeiture. This will usually be the case when even the amount due on allotment has not been received.
